meta.purpose: Proposes the rules by which a candidate axiom is priced (D5 currency), judged (D6 compression predicate), and calibrated against the one existing adoption (D7 FC-W calibration). Adds a decision rule over the prices in import_ledger.json (FTD-0371) and revises none of them.

D5_currency.reporting: stratified vector across the five currencies; NO headline scalar (preserves the FTD-0371 reading guard: the 1 adopted bit is never the total physics import)
D5_currency.predicate_scalar_note: a conservative bit-equivalent used INSIDE the D6 predicate only, never exported as a headline cost

bit_equivalents.cost: log2(|alternatives|); 1 bit if binary; flagged-unknown if the alternative set is open
bit_equivalents.basis: a selection among N discrete options carries log2 N bits
a proven external theorem is a fact, not a choice; it constrains but does not cost
an open result is a conditionality the yield inherits, tracked on the risk side not the cost side
A2 grade-0 closure (FTD-0368; FOUND_DIMENSIONAL_GRADE_CLOSURE.md) shows at least one dimensional anchor is irreducible; a forced floor is not weighed against yield

bit_equivalents.cost: not a cost -- counted on the yield side
bit_equivalents.basis: a bridge is content the axiom licenses, measured in D6

D5_currency.predicate_weighs: structural adoption cost only: adopted-bits + selected-types (bit-equivalents) + any adopted dynamics posit at its declared bit-equivalent
D5_currency.revision_trigger: a candidate whose selected-type has an open (non-enumerable) alternative set cannot be priced until the set is bounded; routes back to the owner

D6_predicate.statement: adopt A only if y(A) > c(A): the licensed structural content, in distinct weighted gap-classes, strictly exceeds the adoption cost in bit-equivalents. y = c is a MARGINAL outcome, admissible only when the single gap-class is high-value (independently checkable, free of tunable parameters), and is flagged marginal.
D6_predicate.index_caveat: y - c and the ordering index y/c are DECISION HEURISTICS, not information-theoretic measures: cost is in bit-equivalents and yield in weighted distinct gap-classes, so the two sides are incommensurable and the index carries no compression-theoretic meaning beyond ranking. It operationalizes the charter's 'explain more than its own degrees of freedom' as a declared rule whose parameters the owner ratifies.
D6_predicate.cost_def: c(A) = structural adoption cost in D5 bit-equivalents, excluding the calibration floor and external dependencies
D6_predicate.yield_def: y(A) = content A licenses that was not licensed before, counted in DISTINCT GAP-CLASSES (not raw rows), weighted by structural strength

yield_weights.kind: [MEASURED] engine signature at a stated protocol

yield_weights.per: -- borrowed form, F10 caution; recorded as consequence, contributes nothing to yield

D6_predicate.weight_note: unit weight credits the conditional content the axiom licenses GIVEN ITSELF (the quantity the compression accounting measures), not substrate-level theorems; it does not assert a [CONDITIONAL THEOREM given a new axiom] has the standing of a substrate [THEOREM]
D6_predicate.anti_gaming: the gap-class unit: rows sharing one mechanism count as ONE gap-class (matches the program metric 'rows counted only with distinct gap-classes named')
guards: a candidate whose entire yield is parametric fails by construction (y = 0) -- blocks adopting an axiom that relabels fitted numbers as content
yield counts only content INDEPENDENT of the candidate's own free parameters -- a candidate cannot pay for itself by licensing restatements of its own posit

D7_fcw_calibration.candidate: FC-W (the adopted alpha-binding law; the delta branch / Z-2 twist)
D7_fcw_calibration.not_an_adjudication: the retro-test does NOT adjudicate FC-W: an owner-declared [AXIOM] is not subject to disqualification by these rules, and because the marginal clause is defined to fit the FC-W point, this is calibration by construction, not independent validation; its purpose is to anchor the floor to a real datum
D7_fcw_calibration.cost_basis: one adopted-bit -- a binary Z/2 orientation the substrate cannot force; the minimal possible structural cost
D7_fcw_calibration.yield_basis: one high-value gap-class in the EM-coupling sector. Two statements stand separately: given W, x+ = 1/alpha as [CONDITIONAL THEOREM given W] (constitution Sec 3.5); the PHYSICAL identification of x+ with the measured fine-structure constant stays [SMC] (FTD-0013, FTD-0386 U-4). High-value because it is the framework's single scan-rigid identification (FTD-0319, a tolerance-conditioned [NUMERICAL FACT], NOT a structural/Bayes result); the constitution records W does no work beyond the alpha-root
D7_fcw_calibration.verdict: MARGINAL point (y = c = 1); the rule takes this as its floor
D7_fcw_calibration.consistency: consistent with -- not a restatement or revision of -- FC-W's standing of record (constitution Sec 3.5: declared-but-conditional, full commitment gated on the [OPEN] condition that W's carrier force independent structural content); the open condition is exactly what would raise y above one gap-class; no tag moves
D7_fcw_calibration.calibration_role: FC-W fixes the scale: 1 bit buying 1 high-value scan-rigid gap-class is the weakest adoption on record; a candidate costing > 1 bit must license proportionally more distinct gap-classes to reach the same point

illustrative_ranking.status: NON-BINDING, NOT owner-ratified; estimates only; each stated yield is itself conditional on proofs not yet built; no candidate has its narrowing theorem or independence proof; authorizes no purchase. Costs price the headline posit as one structural choice (1 bit-equivalent) except the UV distribution, whose many degrees of freedom are counted explicitly. Outcome is against the FC-W floor (index y/c: > 1 pass, = 1 marginal, < 1 fail).

candidates.note: the minimal QM purchase; barred from expanding to wholesale M (AM-5)

candidates.name: matter axiom
candidates.yield_value: consolidates already-priced imports (IMP-S4, IMP-E1 o IMP-E3) into one declared type; no NEW independent content
candidates.note: the tied-cheapest candidate, yet fails: under the independence guard, repackaging already-priced content yields zero new structural content; consolidation may be desirable for bookkeeping but does not pay for itself as yield

illustrative_ranking.yield_individuation_question: The central D6 design question this calibration surfaces: under the conservative default (one posit = one gap-class, no scope weight), every single-posit candidate lands at the marginal point (P6C-C/G/M all y/c = 1), so the predicate separates the two failures but does not rank the three viable candidates. Making it discriminate requires one or both of two declared rulings, neither settleable by the metric: (i) YIELD INDIVIDUATION -- whether distinct phenomena from a single mechanism (P6C-C's confinement vs spectrum) may count as separate gap-classes; (ii) SECTOR SCOPE -- whether breadth of a single sector (P6C-G's whole-gravity yield) counts toward yield, at the cost of a scope weight's own gaming risk. Left unweighted, the predicate rewards multiplicity of distinct mechanisms over breadth of any one, and reports the three viable candidates as a tie.
illustrative_ranking.discrimination_note: two honest, counterintuitive outputs: the most-physics candidate (P6C-U) is weakest because a distribution is expensive, and the tied-cheapest candidate (P6C-F) fails because consolidating priced content yields nothing new. Neither is visible from cost or scope alone.
